h1: Chips Cutter with Stand for Chips Businesses
short_description: Even chips cook evenly, look better and sell better. This chips cutter turns a whole peeled potato into neat, equal chips with one pull of the long lever, so your staff cut a full sack in a fraction of the time it takes by knife. It is a heavy duty potato chips cutter mounted on its own steel stand, made for chips kiosks, takeaways, hotels and schools across Kenya.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Long lever action. The long, rubber-gripped handle multiplies your strength, so one easy pull pushes the potato through the blade. Less effort means your staff keep a steady pace through a busy day.

Square grid blade. The blade cuts every potato into chips of the same thickness, so a batch fries evenly and every portion looks the same. Even chips also use oil more efficiently and come out crisp.

Heavy cast body. The solid metal body stays rigid under pressure and does not wobble, so cutting is safe and the blade stays aligned.

Its own steel stand. The cutter is bolted to a sturdy stand with a tray top that catches chips and water, so you get a dedicated cutting station at the right working height without giving up counter space.

sections.heading: Who It Suits and Where It Is Used
sections.body:
It suits chips kiosks and roadside chips joints, fast food takeaways, hotel and restaurant kitchens, school and college kitchens, and caterers who prepare chips for events.

It pairs naturally with a potato peeler and a chips fryer, giving you a complete chips line from raw potato to plate.

sections.heading: How to Get the Best Chips
sections.body: Peel and wash the potatoes first, and cut off any very long ends so each potato sits flat on the blade. Place the potato on the blade, pull the lever down in one smooth motion and collect the chips in the tray or a basin of clean water. Rinsing cut chips removes surface starch, which helps them fry crisp and stops them sticking together.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying
sections.body: Think about how many potatoes you cut each day and where the cutting station will stand. Make sure the stand sits on a level floor close to your sink and fryer, so peeled potatoes, cut chips and frying follow one short line. Ask us about spare blades and other chip sizes when you order.

sections.heading: Care and Maintenance
sections.body: Rinse the blade and pusher with clean water after every session so starch does not dry on the blade. Dry the cutter before storing it, keep moving parts lightly oiled with food-safe oil, and check the bolts on the stand from time to time. A clean, dry blade stays sharp much longer.
